title: URLResourceKey
observation: Apple exposes file resource, file-system identifier, content identifier, resource type, allocated-size, total-size, volume identifier, and volume-capacity keys as different values.
product_implication: Capture identity, type, allocation, and volume fields separately at scan time and re-read them before action.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. Availability and behavior can change by OS version.

title: fileIdentifierKey
observation: Apple says the internal file identifier is not stable for every file system or across mounts and should not be persisted as a global identity.
product_implication: Use a file identifier only as one short-lived revalidation field and pair it with volume, type, path, and current metadata.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. Availability and behavior can change by OS version.

title: Checking Volume Storage Capacity
observation: Apple separates capacity available for user-requested or required work from capacity available for optional prefetching.
product_implication: Measure the rescue finish line with the capacity value that matches the user's immediate task and keep the measurement source visible.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. Capacity values are dynamic and required-reason API rules can change.

title: NSWorkspace runningApplications
observation: NSWorkspace returns the current running applications and supports observing changes instead of polling.
product_implication: Resolve candidate owners to running applications at review and immediately before action. Do not treat this as proof that no background helper owns the files.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. App identity mapping still needs local validation.

title: NSWorkspace didLaunchApplicationNotification
observation: Apple says launch notifications do not cover background or LSUIElement apps and points to observing runningApplications when all apps matter.
product_implication: A launch-notification-only owner gate is incomplete. Combine live application inventory with process and open-handle checks.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. Notification coverage can change by OS version.

title: NSFilePresenter
observation: File presenters receive coordinated changes, but Apple says direct low-level reads and writes do not notify them.
product_implication: File coordination helps owner-aware actions but cannot prove that no process writes a candidate. Keep open-handle and last-step checks.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. Coordination works only when participating processes use the API.

title: File System Events
observation: FSEvents reports that a directory hierarchy changed and supports per-device streams and extended file identifiers.
product_implication: Use change events to invalidate a saved scan or rescue case, then re-scan exact affected paths before staging or action.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. Events report change, not cleanup safety.

title: Using the File System Events API
observation: Apple documents coalesced directory events and recommends monitoring before scanning, then rescanning directories changed during the scan to avoid missed changes.
product_implication: A scan snapshot needs an invalidation window. Re-scan a candidate if its directory changed during or after classification.
quality_note: Archived first-party Apple guide. Verify API details against the current SDK before implementation.

title: ubiquitousItemDownloadingStatusKey
observation: The iCloud download-status key says whether a local copy exists and whether that copy is the current version.
product_implication: Do not infer local or recoverable state from a path or cloud badge. Read current status and show it before an eviction or handoff.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. This applies to iCloud ubiquitous items, not every File Provider.

title: ubiquitousItemIsUploadedKey
observation: Apple documents a distinct uploaded state and warns not to poll it inside a coordinated-read block because the required read cannot complete until that block returns.
product_implication: Treat upload proof as asynchronous owner state. Do not block a coordinated action while polling for sync completion.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. This applies to iCloud ubiquitous items.

title: ubiquitousItemUploadingError
observation: Apple exposes upload and download errors, unresolved conflicts, upload state, download state, and sharing state as separate ubiquitous-item values.
product_implication: A remote-backed candidate needs explicit sync errors and conflicts in its evidence. A remote copy is not verified when upload failed or conflict state is unresolved.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. This applies to iCloud ubiquitous items.

title: startDownloadingUbiquitousItem
observation: Starting an iCloud download can fetch a missing local copy or synchronize an existing local copy with the cloud version.
product_implication: Describe download as a state-changing owner action with working-space cost. Do not run it as a scan side effect.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. This applies to iCloud ubiquitous items.

title: FileManager iCloud item actions
observation: FileManager exposes different actions for Trash, iCloud local eviction, download, move, copy, replacement, and permanent removal.
product_implication: Represent each action and side effect separately. Generic filesystem deletion must not stand in for local eviction or coordinated replacement.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. Method availability and semantics can change by OS version.

title: setUbiquitous item location
observation: Moving a file into or out of iCloud is a coordinated write that can block, move the physical sandbox file, and requires file-presenter handling for open content.
product_implication: Treat cloud relocation as a supervised owner transaction off the main thread with current state, progress, rollback, and post-action verification.
quality_note: First-party Apple API documentation. This applies to iCloud ubiquitous containers.
